Title: Which novel opens with the words "Call me Ishmael"?
AnswerDetails: Herman Melville's narrator introduces himself with three words before setting out on the whaler Pequod (1851).
OptionD: The Old Man and the Sea

Title: Which novel begins "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife"?
AnswerDetails: Jane Austen's 1813 novel opens with this ironic line, which sets up the Bennet family's marriage plans.

Title: Which Charles Dickens novel opens "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times"?
AnswerDetails: A Tale of Two Cities (1859), set in London and Paris around the French Revolution, opens with this famous run of contrasts.

Title: Which novel begins "Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way"?
AnswerDetails: Leo Tolstoy's Anna Karenina (1878) opens with this line, often quoted as the "Anna Karenina principle."

Title: Which novel opens with Colonel Aureliano Buendía, facing a firing squad, remembering the afternoon his father took him to discover ice?
AnswerDetails: Gabriel García Márquez's 1967 masterpiece opens with this line, which moves across decades in a single sentence.
OptionB: Love in the Time of Cholera

Title: Which novel begins "It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen"?
AnswerDetails: George Orwell's 1949 novel signals from its first sentence that something is wrong with Winston Smith's world.

Title: Which book opens "In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit"?
AnswerDetails: J. R. R. Tolkien said he scribbled the line on a blank page of an exam paper he was marking; The Hobbit followed in 1937.
OptionC: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe

Title: Which story begins "All children, except one, grow up"?
AnswerDetails: It is the first line of J. M. Barrie's novel Peter and Wendy (1911), the book version of his play Peter Pan.

Title: Which novel opens with its narrator unsure whether his mother died "today" or "yesterday"?
AnswerDetails: Albert Camus's The Stranger (L'Étranger, 1942) begins with Meursault's flat report of his mother's death.

Title: In which story does Gregor Samsa wake from uneasy dreams to find himself transformed into a gigantic insect?
AnswerDetails: Franz Kafka's novella The Metamorphosis (1915) begins with the transformation and never explains it.

Title: Who wrote Don Quixote?
AnswerDetails: Miguel de Cervantes published Don Quixote in two parts; it is often called the first modern novel.

Title: Who wrote Things Fall Apart (1958)?
AnswerDetails: The Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe wrote Things Fall Apart, one of the most widely read African novels.

Title: Who wrote Beloved, winner of the 1988 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction?
AnswerDetails: Toni Morrison wrote Beloved (1987) and later won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993.

Title: Who wrote Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus?
AnswerDetails: Mary Shelley was 20 when Frankenstein was published, anonymously, in 1818.

Title: Which poet wrote The Divine Comedy, with its journey through Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso?
AnswerDetails: Dante wrote it in the early 14th century. Virgil appears in the poem as his guide, but did not write it.

Title: Who wrote Madame Bovary?
AnswerDetails: Flaubert was put on trial for obscenity after it was serialized in 1856, was acquitted, and saw the book become a classic.

Title: Who wrote Mrs Dalloway (1925), which follows one day in a London hostess's life?
AnswerDetails: Virginia Woolf's novel follows Clarissa Dalloway as she prepares for a party on a single June day.

Title: Who wrote Midnight's Children, winner of the 1981 Booker Prize?
AnswerDetails: Salman Rushdie's novel follows children born at the moment of India's independence; it later won the Booker of Bookers.

Title: Who wrote The Master and Margarita, in which the Devil visits Soviet Moscow?
AnswerDetails: Bulgakov worked on it until his death in 1940; it was first published, censored, in 1966–67.

Title: Who wrote The Great Gatsby (1925)?
AnswerDetails: F. Scott Fitzgerald's Jazz Age novel follows the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby on Long Island.

Title: In Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird, what is the name of Scout's lawyer father?
AnswerDetails: Atticus Finch defends Tom Robinson in court; Jem is Scout's brother and Boo Radley the reclusive neighbor.

Title: What is the name of Don Quixote's loyal squire?
AnswerDetails: Sancho Panza rides a donkey beside the knight. Rocinante is Don Quixote's horse and Dulcinea his imagined lady.

Title: Which Jules Verne character commands the submarine Nautilus?
AnswerDetails: Captain Nemo appears in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas (1870). Phileas Fogg is Verne's round-the-world traveler.

Title: Who is the impoverished former student at the center of Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment?
AnswerDetails: Raskolnikov drives the 1866 novel. Myshkin is from The Idiot, Ivan from The Brothers Karamazov, Pierre from War and Peace.

Title: Who narrates The Great Gatsby?
AnswerDetails: Nick Carraway, Daisy Buchanan's cousin, rents the house next to Gatsby's and tells the story.

Title: Who is Sherlock Holmes's great criminal adversary, called "the Napoleon of crime"?
AnswerDetails: Arthur Conan Doyle introduced Professor James Moriarty in "The Final Problem" (1893).

Title: In Little Women, which March sister is the aspiring writer?
AnswerDetails: Louisa May Alcott based Jo March, who writes stories and plays, partly on herself.

Title: In Wuthering Heights, which brooding foundling is taken in by the Earnshaw family?
AnswerDetails: Mr. Earnshaw brings Heathcliff home from Liverpool in Emily Brontë's 1847 novel. Rochester belongs to her sister Charlotte's Jane Eyre.

Title: In Homer's Odyssey, who waits faithfully in Ithaca for Odysseus to come home?
AnswerDetails: Penelope holds off her suitors for years, famously unweaving each night the shroud she weaves by day.

Title: In Victor Hugo's Les Misérables, which police inspector relentlessly pursues Jean Valjean?
AnswerDetails: Inspector Javert hunts the former convict Valjean for years; Thénardier is the scheming innkeeper.

Title: James Joyce's Ulysses follows Leopold Bloom through a single day in which city?
AnswerDetails: The novel takes place in Dublin on 16 June 1904, a date fans now celebrate as Bloomsday.

Title: What is the name of the fictional town founded by the Buendía family in One Hundred Years of Solitude?
AnswerDetails: Macondo is García Márquez's town. Comala is from Juan Rulfo's Pedro Páramo and Yoknapatawpha is Faulkner's county.

Title: Thomas Hardy set Tess of the d'Urbervilles and his other major novels in which semi-fictional region of England?
AnswerDetails: Hardy revived the old Anglo-Saxon kingdom name Wessex for his south-west England. Barsetshire is Anthony Trollope's county.

Title: In Khaled Hosseini's The Kite Runner, Amir and Hassan grow up together in which country?
AnswerDetails: The boys fly kites together in 1970s Kabul; the adult Amir later returns to Afghanistan from California.

Title: In John Steinbeck's The Grapes of Wrath, the Joad family leaves Oklahoma for which state?
AnswerDetails: Driven off their farm during the Dust Bowl, the Joads head west along Route 66 to look for work in California.

Title: In Thomas Mann's The Magic Mountain, Hans Castorp stays at a sanatorium in which Swiss resort?
AnswerDetails: Castorp goes to Davos to visit his cousin for three weeks and stays seven years.

Title: Victor Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame is set in which city?
AnswerDetails: The novel is set in 15th-century Paris around the cathedral, and helped spark efforts to preserve it.

Title: Orhan Pamuk's murder mystery My Name Is Red is set among miniature painters in which city?
AnswerDetails: The novel is set in Ottoman Istanbul in the late 16th century. Pamuk won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2006.

Title: In Bram Stoker's Dracula, Jonathan Harker travels to the Count's castle in which region?
AnswerDetails: Harker, a young English solicitor, journeys to Transylvania to finalize the Count's purchase of a house in England.

Title: In which present-day country is Things Fall Apart set?
AnswerDetails: The novel follows Okonkwo in the Igbo village of Umuofia in what is now south-eastern Nigeria.

Title: The Tale of Genji, often called one of the world's first novels, was written about 1,000 years ago in which country?
AnswerDetails: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady-in-waiting at the Japanese imperial court, wrote it in the early 11th century.

Title: In One Thousand and One Nights, who tells stories each night to delay her execution?
AnswerDetails: Scheherazade leaves each tale unfinished at dawn so that King Shahryar spares her for another night.

Title: Which mischievous hero escorts the monk Tang Sanzang in the Chinese classic Journey to the West?
AnswerDetails: Sun Wukong is the star of the 16th-century novel; Guan Yu belongs to Romance of the Three Kingdoms.

Title: The Epic of Gilgamesh, among the oldest surviving works of literature, comes from which ancient civilization?
AnswerDetails: It survives on clay tablets written in cuneiform, telling of a king of the Sumerian city of Uruk.

Title: Leo Tolstoy's War and Peace is set against which conflict?
AnswerDetails: The novel spans 1805 to 1812 and beyond, including Napoleon's invasion of Russia.

Title: In Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's The Little Prince, the narrator is a pilot stranded in which desert?
AnswerDetails: Saint-Exupéry was a pilot himself and had crashed in the Sahara in 1935, years before the book appeared in 1943.

Title: The Bhagavad Gita forms part of which Sanskrit epic?
AnswerDetails: The Gita is a dialogue between Prince Arjuna and Krishna on the eve of the Kurukshetra war in the Mahabharata.

Title: In Goethe's Faust, the restless scholar makes a pact with which devil?
AnswerDetails: Mephistopheles strikes the bargain for Faust's soul; Goethe published Part One in 1808.

Title: Rabindranath Tagore, the first non-European winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913), wrote chiefly in which language?
AnswerDetails: Tagore wrote in Bengali and translated some of his poems, including Gitanjali, into English himself.

Title: Who became the first Arabic-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1988?
AnswerDetails: The Egyptian novelist Naguib Mahfouz is best known for his Cairo Trilogy.

Title: Most of Charles Dickens's novels first reached readers in what form?
AnswerDetails: Dickens published most of his novels in weekly or monthly parts, building suspense from one installment to the next.

Title: Frankenstein began as an entry in a ghost-story challenge proposed by which poet in 1816?
AnswerDetails: At the Villa Diodati near Geneva, Byron suggested that each guest write a ghost story; Mary Shelley's became Frankenstein.

Title: The Victorian novelist "George Eliot," author of Middlemarch, was really which writer?
AnswerDetails: Mary Ann Evans chose a male pen name, partly so that her fiction would be judged on its own terms.

Title: Under which pen name did Charlotte Brontë first publish Jane Eyre in 1847?
AnswerDetails: The three sisters published as Currer (Charlotte), Ellis (Emily) and Acton (Anne) Bell.

Title: Which Russian author's novel Doctor Zhivago was first published in Italy in 1957 after being refused at home?
AnswerDetails: The Milan publisher Feltrinelli brought it out in Italian. Pasternak was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1958 but was forced to decline it.

Title: Kafka's The Trial was published after his death because which friend ignored his request to burn his papers?
AnswerDetails: Max Brod, Kafka's friend and literary executor, published The Trial in 1925 and later The Castle and Amerika.

Title: In which century was the first part of Don Quixote published?
AnswerDetails: Part One appeared in Madrid in 1605 and Part Two in 1615, the year before Cervantes died.

Title: James Joyce's Ulysses was first published as a book in 1922 by the Shakespeare and Company bookshop in which city?
AnswerDetails: Sylvia Beach published it from her Paris bookshop on 2 February 1922, Joyce's 40th birthday.

Title: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote The Hobbit while he was a professor at which university?
AnswerDetails: Tolkien was a professor of Anglo-Saxon at Oxford from 1925, and The Hobbit grew from stories he told his children.

Title: Where did Arthur Conan Doyle stage Sherlock Holmes's apparent death in "The Final Problem" (1893)?
AnswerDetails: Holmes and Moriarty go over the Swiss falls together. Public outcry helped bring Holmes back a decade later.
